title: The Moon Where Kids Only Study at Night
sources: Original fiction (SCIFI world-rule). Real idea used loosely: flickering light can disrupt attention and memory, and sleep helps lock in what you learned (NIH / NIMH sleep and memory notes; NASA notes on twin-star systems).

lines.text: On this moon, kids study at night, and sleep all day.
Study in the daytime, and you forget everything.
Nina landed on Monday, and thought that sounded ridiculous.
The teacher begged her, don't open a book before sunset!
But Nina loved mornings.
So she sat under a tree at ten o'clock, and studied.
And that wasn't the strange part.
By lunch, she forgot her own name.
Then she forgot the whole alphabet. Twice.
Her classmates watched through the window, hugging their pillows.
By noon, her notebook was blank, and so was her face.
The teacher sighed. Told you.
But Nina squinted at the sky, and noticed something.
See, this moon's twin suns flicker forty times a second,
and that flicker scrambles your short-term memory.
So she put on dark crystal glasses,
and studied all day, in full sunshine.
She topped the entire school.
And the teacher? He borrowed her glasses.
Which is why, on this moon,
